Strict equivariance rarely holds in real data, and forcing it can hurt accuracy. Their method projects a pretrained model's weights into a chosen subspace to set the softness level. The plan works on any pretrained design and comes with theory bounding the induced error. On ViT and ResNet backbones it lifts results across classification, segmentation, and trajectory tasks. On ImageNet it improves accuracy while also cutting equivariance error.
arxiv-2603-26957: Gaitsgory and co-authors apply higher categorical trace methods to Deligne-Lusztig theory. This work is the second part of a series on categorical traces. It uses the AGCat two-category formalism developed in the authors' earlier joint work. The operation of higher categorical trace is the central tool. With it, they re-derive a number of known results in Deligne-Lusztig theory. The paper shows the trace machinery reaching a classical area of representation theory. The re-derivations display the formalism working inside a classical domain.
arxiv-2603-27157: Prajapati and Srivastava build gauge models that give a Z' boson purely axial or mixed couplings. Simple extensions like B-L naturally yield only vector-like Z' interactions. Their new class uses flavor-specific chiral U(1)X symmetries instead. Three right-handed neutrinos cancel the gauge anomalies. The authors classify anomaly-free charge assignments. Quark and lepton charges can differ sharply within one model. That non-universality creates flavor-changing neutral currents in both sectors. Benchmark models show axial couplings arise for heavy and light Z' bosons alike.
arxiv-2603-27257: Xue links the birth of matter, magnetism, and dark matter to one early-universe story. Gravity-produced superheavy particle-antiparticle pairs swing quantum mechanically during reheating. Density perturbations between the partners cross outside the horizon as the universe expands. That leaves a particle excess inside the horizon once the heavy states decay. Their decays into light baryons and leptons explain baryogenesis and leptogenesis. Charged decay products drive currents that seed a primordial magnetic field. The ratios and field bounds fit data. A parallel dark-sector asymmetry, darkogenesis, is also treated.
arxiv-2603-27357: Kraicer and co-authors guide lensless polarization imaging with an ordinary RGB camera for sharper results. Polarization reveals cues the eye misses, but proper cameras are pricey and bulky. Lensless designs swap the lens for a diffuser and rebuild images computationally. Their system pairs a compact polarization-RGB sensor with a standard RGB camera. A physics-based inversion first recovers a rough polarization image per color channel. A transformer fusion network then refines it using the RGB guidance. Quality beat lensless-only baselines across datasets and conditions.
arxiv-2603-27457: Fan and co-authors tackle unmixing blended data distributions. Each group of samples mixes the same hidden densities in new shares. The task is to recover each hidden density. Their method adapts kernel density estimation with group weights. Weights come from topic-style fits on histogram data. A U-statistic step removes bias from those weights. Error rates match a proven lower bound, so the method is optimal. The problem extends topic modeling to smooth data. It also applies to word embedding models.
arxiv-2603-27557: Pham and co-authors ask what makes a fake-speech detector work broadly. Two factors matter: real speech sources and fake generators. A model trained on skewed mixes fails on new sets. The team first builds a baseline detector. Tests show how each factor moves the decision threshold. They then build a balanced dataset from public sets. Models trained on it score well across benchmarks. Balance, they conclude, is the key to general detection.
arxiv-2603-27657: Mutuk and Kang compute magnetic moments of heavy pentaquark molecules. The states mix bottom and charm quarks with light ones. Each state is modeled as a baryon bound to a meson. Two octet families arise from diquark symmetry types. Spin-flavor wavefunctions are built for both families. Moments follow within the constituent quark model. One family shows near-universal moment values. A spin-singlet diquark explains that flat pattern.
arxiv-2603-27757: Sen and co-authors forecast motion from event camera streams. Event cameras log brightness changes pixel by pixel. The data are sparse yet rich in timing. E-TIDE predicts future event tensors from past ones. A TIDE module captures time links in sparse tensors. The design stays light and trains end to end. No large-scale pretraining is needed. Downstream tasks like future segmentation stand to gain.
arxiv-2603-27857: Kalafatelis and co-authors coordinate shipboard learning without a central server. Vessels hold sensitive data with patchy links at sea. CARGO splits learning into control and data planes. The data plane trains locally with compressed gossip. The control plane picks ships and links each round. Compression strength is also set there. Carbon cost, reliability, and fairness all guide choices. Recovery actions trigger when rounds go wrong.
arxiv-2603-28157: Golonka and Maciejewski ask how many hot Jupiters are spiraling toward their stars through tidal wave breaking. They recompute star traits for 550 systems and feed them through stellar models to get decay rates. Wave breaking stays off in young stars, and about 43% of the planets should inspiral on the main sequence. The shortest-period planets, oddly, are safe from this fate. Clear timing proof may take decades, but population patterns should show sooner.
arxiv-2603-28257: Breazu builds KAN-PCA, a nonlinear twist on principal component analysis for asset returns. Each edge of his autoencoder uses a learned spline from a Kolmogorov-Arnold network, while the decoder stays linear. He proves that forcing the splines linear returns plain PCA exactly. On 20 S&P 500 stocks over a decade, three factors rebuilt returns with an R-squared of 66.57%, against 62.99% for PCA. Out-of-sample results matched after a leakage fix.
arxiv-2603-28357: Vu classifies brain tumors in MRI scans with a weighted voting ensemble of many models. The system mixes deep networks, among them ResNet and DenseNet variants, with classic tools like SVM and KNN on hand-crafted features. Each model votes with a weight set by its own accuracy. Contrast balancing, clustering, and edge detection clean the images first. On Figshare and Kaggle MRI data, the ensemble beat existing models and reached top accuracy.
arxiv-2603-28457: Akemann and six co-authors compare local statistics at the edges of three non-Hermitian random matrix classes. They study complex spacing ratios and nearest-neighbor gaps for the Ginibre, symmetric, and self-dual ensembles. In the first class they clean up exact finite-size formulas and test a three-by-three guess that bends toward the unitary case. Numerical work across all three classes matches a picture of charges repelling in a two-dimensional Coulomb gas. The spacing ratio alone, they find, misses some edge detail.
arxiv-2603-28557: Moura and Silva study charged, accelerating black holes in the eikonal limit. They show that quasinormal modes link to the angular speed of circular light paths. The modes also link to a Lyapunov exponent, as for spherically symmetric black holes. They compute greybody factors for neutral and charged cases with massless scalar fields. They report that the results hold for perturbations of any spin. They also find the radius of the shadow cast by such black holes. Setting acceleration to zero recovers the Reissner-Nordstrom case.
arxiv-2603-28957: Falcone and Das introduce GF pastamarkers, an extension of the pastamarkers plotting package that uses gluten free pasta as data markers. The PASTA Collaboration built pastamarkers to make plots more engaging with pasta shaped markers. Gluten free pasta has a fragile structure, which the new package turns into a feature. An exponential crumbling factor rewards authors for clearer, more concise articles. The stated aim is to serve the gluten free population while boosting productivity. Shorter, clearer manuscripts and proposals are the intended side effect.
arxiv-2603-29157: Diamond studies sextic fourfolds built from ternary sextic polynomials. The Shioda construction attaches a smooth fourfold to each such polynomial. An involution acts on the fourfold and fixes a Hodge substructure. That substructure has Hodge coniveau one. The general Hodge conjecture predicts a divisor tied to this substructure. Diamond verifies the prediction when the polynomial has minimum Waring rank. The result partly answers a question posed by Voisin. The work links explicit geometry with a deep conjecture.
arxiv-2603-29257: Zhou and co-authors present a GPU version of time-dependent density functional theory for large molecules. Their minimal auxiliary basis method runs in GPU4PySCF. Tricks include fast three-center integrals and exchange-space truncation. Hydrogen atoms are dropped from the auxiliary basis. A memory-assisted Davidson solver helps on the host side. On a benchmark set, excitation errors stayed near 0.03 to 0.05 electron volts. Systems up to 3,000 atoms finished on one A100 GPU. Times ranged from minutes to hours.
arxiv-2603-29357: Sha and Zhao ask how many independent signals a benchmark really gives. Score suites often report many numbers that repeat the same information. They define Effective Dimensionality from the spectrum of benchmark scores. It acts as a fast upper-bound check on measurement breadth. They applied it to 22 benchmarks and over 8,400 model runs. The six-score Open LLM Leaderboard behaved like about two axes. BBH and MMLU-Pro carried near-identical signal. The authors release an atlas and a four-step workflow.
arxiv-2604-00057: Zeyu Jin and four colleagues present GameSight, a two-stage system that writes soccer commentary in live-television style rather than anonymous play-by-play text. It first ties unnamed figures in video to specific players and teams through visual reasoning, then enriches the draft with historical statistics and the evolving game state. On the SN-Caption-test-align set, player alignment accuracy rises 18.5 percent above Gemini 2.5-pro, alongside better segment accuracy and game-level relevance.
arxiv-2604-00257: Hughes and de Jong show that an expanding toral endomorphism has a Markov partition whose boundary is piecewise smooth exactly when a power of its inducing matrix diagonalizes with integer eigenvalues. Such a boundary must in fact be piecewise linear, not merely smooth. In dimension 2, they add subtler findings about boundary smoothness. They also give an upper bound on the Hausdorff dimension.
arxiv-2604-00357: Jiang and colleagues report a striking mismatch in the microquasar GRS 1915+105, observed with the East Asian VLBI network in April 2023. The steady jet kept its long-standing direction near 147 degrees, while discrete blobs flew out near 188 degrees, the slowest such outflow yet recorded at about 0.35 times light speed. A repeat mismatch months later points to a shifting launch geometry, plausibly a warped accretion disk.
arxiv-2604-00557: Xie and colleagues scale camera views to make robot imitation learning data-efficient. Imitation policies live or die by the variety of expert demos, yet gathering demos across varied settings costs much and proves hard. Their framework uses scene variety already present, without extra human effort, by adding camera views during demo collection. Several synced camera angles turn each expert path into pseudo-demos, enriching training data and improving viewpoint invariance. Camera-space action encodings add further variety.
arxiv-2604-00657: Wang and colleagues present LibScan, a detector for smart-contract library misuse. Smart contracts are programs managing financial transactions on blockchains, and developers lean on outside libraries for efficiency and security. Improper library use can hide vulnerabilities that are hard to detect and costly in money losses. Existing tools struggle because misuse often needs grasping coder intent, not just scanning for known patterns. LibScan joins language-model meaning analysis with rule-based code checks, spotting eight distinct misuse categories, and adds iterative self-correction to improve reliability.
arxiv-2604-00957: Eiter, Lasarzik, and Wiedemann compare broad solution ideas for nonlinear fluid-flow PDE systems: measure-valued, dissipative weak, and energy-variational solutions. For incompressible Euler flows, they prove all three ideas match when the energy rule is framed the right way. For several fluid-flow conservation-law cases, they show the energy-variational notion matches suitably refined dissipative weak ones, with defect measures sharply capped by the energy defect. Their cases include compressible isentropic Euler, Euler-Korteweg, and Euler-Poisson systems.
arxiv-2604-01257: Imomov and colleagues refine limit theorems for continuous-time Markov branching-immigration systems. Branching systems, used across biology, physics, and finance, evolve in continuous time with transitions to multiple states from a single state, so change and branching must be handled together. The paper investigates long-term behavior of transition functions, setting convergence rates and better asymptotic expansions under looser moment conditions. The results deepen understanding of long-term behavior and stable patterns in these systems.
arxiv-2604-01457: Zhao and colleagues analyse high verbalized confidence in language models. It has three axes: tracing it as a gradient-friendly internal signal, finding the circuits that inflate it, and using these insights for test-time recalibration. Across two tuned language models on three test sets, a set of MLP blocks and attention heads, concentrated in middle-to-late layers, writes the confidence-inflation signal at the token position. Interventions on these circuits substantially improve calibration. Results suggest overconfidence is driven by identifiable circuits and can be mitigated through targeted intervention.
arxiv-2604-01557: Chen and colleagues complement a lower bound on relative-error testing of halfspaces. They show halfspaces can be relative-error tested over real space under the Gaussian distribution with sublinear oracle calls. The relative-error model measures distance from target to candidate as disagreeing inputs divided by satisfying inputs. This suits sparse Boolean-valued functions where only a small fraction of assignments satisfy the function. Recent work showed that over the Boolean domain, any relative-error test for halfspaces, or linear threshold functions, needs logarithmically many oracle calls in n.
arxiv-2604-01657: Rao and Callison-Burch generate reasoning traces for 24K claim checks across 9 datasets with GPT-4o-mini. Direct evidence extraction leads by far; multi-sentence synthesis and number reasoning show up seldom. Datasets differ starkly: some lean on lexical matching, while others demand information synthesis in about half their cases. Using a compact 1B checker, they list five errors: general-domain checks show lexical overlap bias, scientific checks overcautiousness, and mathematical checks arithmetic reasoning failures. High benchmark scores seem to mostly reflect retrieval-plus-entailment ability.
arxiv-2604-01757: Serret and colleagues survey attention methods through a numerical lens, addressing the quadratic cost in input length slowing large-scale use. They review and sort fast shortcut methods by numerical idea: gaps and grouping, low-rank and subspace mapping, random sketches, and tensor splits. They also discuss kernel-inspired rewrites and recent forms, such as Latent Attention, modifying the standard softmax formula for speed. Presenting these developments in one math frame, they aim to bridge fields and highlight chances for numerical linear algebra in building large attention methods.
arxiv-2604-01957: Thellmann, Stadler and Färber audit translation quality in the EU20 suite, five benchmarks rendered into 20 languages. Machine translation cuts cost and scales fast, but noise, lost structure and uneven quality weaken trust. Their three step automated check covers a structural corpus audit with fixes, COMET profiling across DeepL, ChatGPT and Google, and a language-model scan of span level errors. Lower COMET scores tracked more accuracy and mistranslation errors, notably in HellaSwag, while ARC stayed cleaner, and the team released cleaned datasets and code to focus review.
arxiv-2604-02057: Sunil, Benali and Moutuou map how synaptic and extrasynaptic signaling organize brain function in Caenorhabditis elegans, from synapse and neuropeptide maps. They infer flow with equilibrium physics, comparing it with the diffuse layer. Four regimes emerge: a wiring dependent layer backing motor circuits, and a resilient layer guiding regulation and control. A diffuse network sustains survival and balance, and a wired regime handles sense and motion. The two modes are tuned for speed, control, toughness and survival.
arxiv-2604-02457: Kalidasu and team test a street legal real world attack on plate readers. Their Street legal Physical Adversarial Rim fits around a plate without changing or hiding it, fooling a modern open source reader system. Under optimal setup it cuts reader scores by 60 percent and hits an 18 percent mimicry rate. Built for under 100 dollars by paid coding aides, it needs no access to reader systems during use. The authors argue from law and case law that the rim is street legal in Texas, showing real flaws in modern readers.
arxiv-2604-03057: Hontan and three colleagues present an open-source method for querying structured non-textual data sets in natural language. Retrieval-augmented methods struggle with numerical and structured information, so the team trains a language model to generate executable queries instead. A planned pipeline creates synthetic training data with diverse question-answer pairs capturing intent and dataset semantics. They fine-tune DeepSeek R1 Distill 8B with QLoRA and 4-bit quantization for common hardware. Tested on service-access data for Durangaldea, the model scores highly in monolingual, multilingual, and unseen-location settings.
arxiv-2604-03257: Shen and colleagues offer a rigorous way to estimate how often language models fail, without relying only on costly human labels or biased machine judges. Their constrained maximum-likelihood method combines a small human calibration set, a large judge-annotated corpus, and side constraints from known judge-performance bounds. Across varied regimes, it beats prediction-powered inference with more accurate, lower-variance estimates.
arxiv-2604-03457: Blanes and Escorihuela-Tomàs show that D-splitting methods on a wider phase space work as fast two-slot explicit Runge-Kutta methods without a third slot. The methods preserve key traits of exact answers beyond their formal order, earning the pseudo-geometric label. New tailored methods built from their traits are tested on examples.
arxiv-2604-03557: Dai and colleagues model next-token guessing as graph search, where entities are nodes and learned links are edges, to explain reasoning hallucinations in large language models. Context-bound thinking becomes constrained search over a sampled subgraph, while context-free queries lean on stored structures. These failures arise from two causes. Path Reuse means stored knowledge beats context early in training, while Path Compression collapses frequent multi-step paths into shortcut edges later.
arxiv-2604-03657: Luo and colleagues show that image in-context learning prompts chosen for image likeness alone can be label-mismatched and degrade scores. They develop LaPR, a label-aware prompt picking framework that builds an image-label joint code for prompts. It uses a mixture-of-experts setup with query-tuned routing for missing query labels. LaPR improves in-context cutting, spotting, and tinting, and carries over across feature pullers and cross-fold setups.
arxiv-2604-03757: Bonitz and colleagues surveyed where quantum effects matter in plasmas, from warm dense matter to inertial fusion. They opened with the history, noting 2025 as UNESCO's International Year of Quantum Science and Technology, then mapped the broad parameter ranges of plasmas and the experiments where quantum behavior rules. The review weighs theoretical tools for dense plasmas and argues that a downfolding approach built on first-principles simulations holds the key to prediction.
arxiv-2604-03857: Xiaoxuan Qin and colleagues tested whether large language models can steer internet congestion control. Phase one isolated the model to the congestion-avoidance phase, pinning down when to call it, what to feed it, and how to phrase its instructions. Phase two widened its role into a general policy across control phases. On static and dynamic traces, the model policy cut latency by up to 50 percent with less than 0.3 percent throughput loss.
arxiv-2604-04257: Tian studies frame operators built from cylinder indicator functions for the Bernoulli Cantor measure. When the parameter equals one half, Haar differences diagonalize the operators. For other values between zero and one, the weighted Haar basis still gives a sparse tree-banded matrix, though diagonalization is lost. Tian also proves a filtration picture from conditional expectations and level-wise mass operators. That picture yields a limit operator that is compact, positive and self-adjoint, fixed by a self-similar identity from the first Cantor split, with matching resolvent formulas.
arxiv-2604-04357: Han and colleagues present SW-CLIP, a framework for street-view geo-localization that builds spatial reasoning into contrastive learning. Standard CLIP treats every non-matching sample as equally negative, ignoring geography. SW-CLIP instead applies Tobler's First Law, modelling place relations by distance. It encodes places as text, swaps one-hot targets for soft labels from geodesic distance, and adds neighbourhood regularization to preserve local structure. On a multi-city dataset it beats standard CLIP on accuracy, long-tail errors and coherence, arguing for geographic over purely semantic alignment.
arxiv-2604-04457: Yue and colleagues present RAR, a retrieval-aided chat recommender aligning search and generation to improve scores and cut errors. Large language models now serve as chat recommenders, but existing methods rely on pretrained knowledge alone. The team builds a movie corpus of over 300,000 titles with metadata. A finder first picks options from user history, and a language model refines them with conversational context. RL feedback updates the finder toward higher-ranking option sets. Tests on multiple benchmarks show RAR beats state-of-the-art baselines.
arxiv-2604-04857: Mao and five colleagues examine a paradox in self-driving vision-language models: fine-tuning them on driving data can erase the broad world knowledge that made them useful. They build a 180,000-scene dataset and the first benchmark for measuring this forgetting in driving models, showing that current methods lose much prior knowledge. Their Drive Expert Adapter instead routes each scene through specialist experts in prompt space, lifting driving performance without rewriting the core weights.
arxiv-2604-04957: Liang and thirteen co-authors present FluxMC, a machine-learning framework for Bayesian inference in space gravitational-wave work. Detailed physical modeling clashes with random sampling limits, since complex spaces trap standard Monte Carlo methods in costly likelihood checks and local optima. FluxMC combines flow matching with parallel tempering Monte Carlo, shifting inference from local search to guided transport. It joins generative foresight with proven convergence, aiming for rapid inference where older samplers stall.
arxiv-2604-05057: Pal, Bhattacharya, and Singh propose blind-spot mass, a Good-Turing framework for quantifying deployment coverage risk in machine learning. Operational states are often heavy-tailed, so a long tail of valid but rare states stays under-supported in finite training and evaluation data. Models can therefore look accurate on standard test sets yet stay unreliable across large regions of deployment space. Blind-spot mass estimates the total probability assigned to states whose empirical support falls below a threshold, using Good-Turing unseen-species estimation to measure uncovered distribution.
arxiv-2604-05157: Chen and five colleagues propose IntentScore, a reward model that scores actions for computer-use agents. Such agents use large language models to run desktop tasks without judging action quality, so errors cascade. IntentScore learns from 398K offline GUI steps, using contrastive alignment for relevance and margin ranking for correctness. It embeds each planning intent, telling apart similar actions with different rationales. On tests it reaches 97.5 percent accuracy, and reranking Agent S3 on unseen OSWorld it lifts task success by 6.9 points.
arxiv-2604-05257: Dobhal, Garcia, and Inoue propose an add-on of TabDDPM, adding sense through time plugs and modules. TabDDPM makes fake data from sets but assumes solo samples, blocking use for time domains. Shaping data into runs and using via time codes, action labels, and missing masks enables fake runs. Tests with grids and links shows better realism, range, and flow. On WISDM data, the system gives series like sensor patterns at macro F1-score 0.64 and scores 0.71, aiding classes and match.
arxiv-2604-05657: Gómez-Martínez and Requeno Jarabo compute reachability graphs for Petri net product lines without enumerating every product. Symbolic state encodings plus family-preserving successor generation capture all variants in one compact parameterized graph, with merging and abstraction curbing state explosion. Proofs of soundness and completeness back the method, and tool tests show large memory and time savings.
arxiv-2604-06057: Gutwein and Wang's 2026 paper studies the moduli space of conically singular instantons over a six-dimensional SU(3) space. They build a Fredholm deformation theory fixing the tangent connection while varying the bundle and singular set. That yields a Kuranishi structure for the moduli space. They also study the cokernel of the deformation operator and give its dimension formula under certain assumptions. Finally, they apply the results to such instantons with structure group PU(n). That gives a virtual dimension formula in terms of sheaf cohomology over the projective plane.
arxiv-2604-06157: Coleman and three colleagues model a fractionalized Fermi liquid on a square lattice. Conduction electrons interact with a Yao-Lee spin liquid carrying a Majorana Fermi surface, while a static gauge theory keeps the model solvable. Two phases appear: one where spin-liquid fermions merge with conduction electrons into a Fermi surface that breaks the Luttinger count, and one where they stay separate. The small-surface phase yields coherence factors behind Fermi arcs, plus a diamagnetic response and a diverging Sommerfeld coefficient at the pseudogap onset.
arxiv-2604-06357: English and Spiro prove a sweeping result for generalized Turán problems, counting the most copies of a graph T inside a larger graph with no forbidden pattern F. For any tree, graph family, and integer k, the count either grows at least like n to the power k plus one. Or it stays bounded by the ordinary Turán number raised to k. Their proofs build new tree versions of the classical Helly theorem, of independent interest beyond this first Helly-theorem use on Turán-type problems.
arxiv-2604-06657: Zhang, Yao, Yang, and Mei tackle freshness in cell-free massive MIMO networks with S&C sharing infrastructure. Splitting access points between sensing and message work trades update generation against sound short-packet sends. Their unified framework joins random geometry with random network math to map peak age-of-information breach odds. Working out timing functions under fuzzy channel knowledge and short-block coding yields a usable cap, whose best split matches sim tests closely.
arxiv-2604-06857: Zhao and Feng separate storm-time shielding effects from Forbush decreases in cosmic-ray data. Forbush decreases briefly cut galactic cosmic-ray flux after solar disturbances, and storm-time shifts in cutoff rigidity can raise or lower ground count rates. Using hourly proton flux rebuilt from neutron-monitor data for May 2011 through October 2019, they show local anomalies can reach 1 GV, biasing rigidity links inferred during disturbed intervals. Since AMS measures proton rigidity in space, its daily spectrum offers a stable guide for corrections that remove glitches while keeping broader evolution.
arxiv-2604-07057: Saputra and four colleagues build a tool that judges the mood of Indonesian text only after it reads the topic the text is about. Most older tools read a line on its own, so they miss cases where the same words mean praise on one topic and blame on another. Their tool, IndoBERT-Sentiment, takes topic and text as input and was trained on more than thirty one thousand pairs across nearly two hundred topics. In tests it beat the best widely used Indonesian tool by a wide margin.
arxiv-2604-07357: Gheffari, Benouddane, and Silarbi build an Arabic speech emotion recognizer from a hybrid convolutional-transformer network. Arabic emotion data is scarce, so the work targets a low-resource language where English and European systems do not transfer directly. Convolutional layers pull spectral features from Mel-spectrograms, while transformer encoders track long-range timing patterns in speech. On the Egyptian Arabic EYASE corpus, the model reaches 97.8 percent accuracy with a macro F1 score of 0.98, showing the hybrid design's strength for Arabic emotion recognition.
arxiv-2604-07557: Varner and four colleagues present multiplicity-weighted Stochastic Attention for synthetic patient generation. It is a new system based on modern Hopfield networks for small long-term cohorts. It stores real patient cases as memory patterns in a smooth energy landscape. The result is a finite mixture with one part per stored case. These weights amplify picked subgroups at use time with no new training. Applied to clotting data from 23 patients while pregnant, made cases closely matched real ones.
arxiv-2604-07657: Montenegro and two colleagues extend a Gaussian fluid theory with torsion as an extra field, building fluctuating fluid dynamics with spin. The theory stays covariant under pseudo-gauge changes and under foliations. Second-order gravitational Ward identities, derived here with torsion, secure the result. While spin observables depend on the pseudo-gauge, the dynamics stays independent of it, clarifying the pseudo-gauge's role in spin fluids.
arxiv-2604-07957: Chen and six colleagues present WorldMAP, a teacher-student framework for vision-language navigation trajectory prediction. Vision-language models increasingly plan or predict paths, while generative world models imagine future views for look-ahead reasoning. Predicting a reliable path from one egocentric view remains hard: current models produce unstable paths, and imagined futures do not supply grounded learning signals. WorldMAP converts world-model-generated futures into lasting semantic-spatial structure plus planning-derived supervision. The grounded supervision aims for stable paths from single views.
arxiv-2604-08057: Dekkers and eight colleagues introduce orthogonalised self-guided quantum tomography, inspired by single-pixel imaging. Self-guided imaging serves as a linear analogue of self-guided quantum tomography and matches single-pixel imaging. Borrowing from ghost imaging, a recent advance in single-pixel imaging, the team introduces orthogonalised tomography. The method needs no extra test overhead and converges faster and more accurately. Numerical fidelity rises from about 95 percent to about 99 percent, while test fidelity rises from about 92 percent to about 95 percent, showing routines can interchange between the two fields.
arxiv-2604-08357: Le Cleï, Thuerey, and Zhu improve diffusion models that stand in for fluid and flow equations over time. Standard noise plans, they show, leave needless rebuilding error and make long training runs costly. Their adaptive plan caps the bias from training exposure to cut that error, and a cheaper proxy training pass steadies long forecasts. Tests on forced flow, wave, and transonic cases beat diffusion and deterministic rivals on short accuracy and long stability.
arxiv-2604-08457: Gan and six colleagues present CrashSight, a benchmark for understanding road crashes from roadside cameras rather than from the car itself. It holds 250 crash videos with 13,000 multiple choice questions in two tiers: scene grounding first, then crash mechanics, causes, timing, and aftermath. Eight leading vision language models describe scenes well but stumble on temporal and causal reasoning in safety critical cases.
arxiv-2604-08557: Singh breaks safety alignment in diffusion language models by re masking committed refusal tokens and adding a short affirmative prefix. The TrajHijack attack reaches 74 to 82 percent success on HarmBench across three safety tuned models, rising to 92 to 98 percent with a generic eight token compliance prefix. Neither trick works alone, gradient tuning hurts the attack, and the strongest published defense proves even more vulnerable, an effect he calls defense inversion.
arxiv-2604-08657: Lee, Ramos, and Vilches ask how well the QCD axion can hide when several axion fields interact. Level crossings and string bundles shift the axion's mass and couplings, and the domain wall bound on its photon coupling can relax in multi axion settings. The axion may carry only part of the dark matter. Even so, in most regions where it evades detection, an axion like particle stays visible to next generation experiments. The best search regions are mapped in a two axion example.
arxiv-2604-08757: Fettach and three colleagues benchmark humor alignment in language models by having five frontier models play Cards Against Humanity like human players. Across 9,894 rounds, models pick the funniest card from ten options, beating chance yet aligning only modestly with human taste. Strikingly, models agree with each other far more than with humans. Position biases and content preferences partly explain the pattern, raising doubts about whether model humor reflects real preference or inference artifacts.
arxiv-2604-09057: Liao and seven colleagues present Tora3, a trajectory-guided system for generating audio and video together with coherent motion and sound. Existing methods often produce shaky motion and loosely tied sounds, because video and audio generation share no explicit motion-aware structure. Tora3 guides both streams with trajectories, keeping fidelity in conditioned regions and local coherence elsewhere. The team curates PAV, a large audio-video dataset stressing motion patterns with automatic motion labels. Tests show gains in motion realism, motion-sound synchronization, and overall quality over strong open-source baselines.
arxiv-2604-09157: Pham and five colleagues present Energy-Shifting for fast Monte Carlo dose calculation in radiotherapy. The method uses deep learning to build complex polyenergetic dose distributions from simple monoenergetic inputs under same beam configurations. Unlike denoising methods that rely on noisy low-count dose maps, it works better on new data. The method keeps precision and structural preservation with speed fit for real-time use. It reaches a gamma passing rate over 98 percent under a 3 percent, 3 millimeter criterion against the Monte Carlo reference, for prostate planning.
arxiv-2604-09357: Ferraro, Naves, and Larson present discrete-time quantum walks in model dimensions, on Fock-state lattices. Such grids suit lattice models, mainly in quantum optical systems, unlike the usual real-space or phase-space walker. Their Lie-algebra method links a phase space and a Fock-state lattice to each algebra, yielding the walk's discrete unitary tool via shift operators. They replace nearest-neighbor shifts, causing state-linked hopping, and cases show fast spreading, linkage, mixing, super-fast spreading, and trapping.
arxiv-2604-09557: Abramovich and seven colleagues standardize how speculative decoding is measured. The technique's speed gains depend heavily on the data it runs on. Their SPEED-Bench suite pairs two splits. A qualitative split is chosen for semantic variety, while a throughput split spans low-batch latency tests to high-load runs. Built to plug into production engines such as vLLM and TensorRT-LLM, it exposes behaviors other benchmarks hide. Synthetic inputs flatter real throughput, draft lengths shift with batch size, and narrow data biases results.
arxiv-2604-09957: Hewage, Chakkravarthy, and Abeysekara show putting partial change rules into tunable quantum circuit loss functions eases barren plateaus, where gradients vanish with system size. Gradient-variance lower bounds show physics-bound losses built from local equation gaps inherit good power scaling, while focus gathers gradient information. Tests on the heat, Burgers, and shallow-water rules across 4 to 8 qubits and 1 to 5 layers show physics-bound circuits resist fast gradient fading. Shaped ansatze run in a sub-maximal link regime, and physics-bound circuits reach lower loss in fewer epochs.
arxiv-2604-10157: Basu speeds dopant screening for oxide semiconductors, where doping tunes band gaps for photocatalysis. Screening five oxide hosts, he runs a zinc oxide co-doping campaign. Copper-bearing co-doped zinc oxide hits visible-light band gaps, with Y2Cu2 co-doped zinc oxide best at 1.84 electron volts. A three-tier validation funnel shows no single theory level suffices. A multi-fidelity strategy replaces 81 percent of density functional evaluations with surrogates, cutting 440 CPU-hours to 62 and finding the global optimum in all 50 trials.
arxiv-2604-10257: Chen and 15 colleagues propose DREAMuS, a fixed-target experiment at the heavy-ion facility HIAF to hunt muon-philic dark matter. The target is dark matter mediated by a light flavor-violating boson, a vector Z-prime or scalar phi made when muons strike nuclei, decaying into dark matter. Precision tracking and time-of-flight suppress Standard Model backgrounds. DREAMuS reaches competitive sensitivity for GeV-scale muon-philic dark matter, down to couplings of one part in ten thousand. A complementary positive-muon beam could improve sensitivity below 200 MeV tenfold.
arxiv-2604-10357: Zhou, Zhang, Arivoli, and Negrut build a graphics chip version of a flexible body physics code. The code handles bendy parts that deform a lot, using ten node tetrahedra plus beam and shell pieces. Time steps use a backward Euler scheme, and limits are held by an augmented Lagrange loop. Two chip parallel schemes speed force and stiffness work, with AdamW and Newton inner solvers. At the largest meshes, the Newton solver runs about ten times faster than CPU baselines.
arxiv-2604-10857: Xun and Price prove the first lower bounds on score queries for diffusion sampling. In diffusion sampling, models generate samples by repeatedly querying learned score estimates. For d-dimensional distributions with score estimates of polynomial accuracy, they show any sampling method needs on the order of the square root of d adaptive queries. Within any polynomial total-query budget, success must search over a similar number of distinct noise levels. This formally explains why multiscale noise schedules are needed in practice.
arxiv-2604-10957: Fukui compiles a global database of three hundred writing systems, fifty binary structural traits, and two hundred fifty-nine family-tree edges spanning fifty-four centuries. He studies scripts as cultural copies, using tree-building, Bayesian, and neural methods. Scripts show a detectable molecular clock, but political intervention breaks it. Divergence gaps track intervention intensity. He lists thirty major script replacement events. Colonial contact predicts script extinction. The Spanish Empire extinguished the most contacted scripts, six of twelve, followed by Japan with three of nine.
arxiv-2604-11057: Ly and Hayami show that a noncollinear kagome antiferromagnet can generate flipping out-of-plane spin polarization from spin chirality, without spin-orbit coupling. Spatial confinement makes the system develop spin separation patterns governed by termination symmetry. Breaking the side mirror symmetry of the ribbon produces altermagnetic-like spin splitting across the band structure. The authors also uncover spin-edge locking, in which moving edge states acquire unusual spin pattern. These results show how magnet shape and trapping can generate spin-polarized transport in coplanar magnets without relativistic interactions.
arxiv-2604-11457: Shaltiel and Sharon measure 3D turbulence in a rapidly rotating fluid in fine detail. Splitting the flow into a vertically averaged part and a 3D residual, they find the quasi-2D component dominates low frequencies and the 3D component higher ones. That split, however, is not intrinsic to the flow. As the vertical scan range grows, the crossover shifts steadily. The findings challenge the notion of a pure 2D manifold in rotating turbulence theory. They call for frameworks accounting for scan-dependent structure and wave-vortex coupling.
arxiv-2604-11557: Liang and seven colleagues present UniToolCall, a unified framework for tool learning in LLM agents. It sets one standard for toolsets, datasets, and tests, curating over 22,000 tools and a hybrid set of over 390,000 cases from 10 public datasets plus synthetic runs. An Anchor Linkage mechanism ties turns together, and seven public benchmarks are recast in a unified Query-Action-Observation-Answer form. Fine-tuned Qwen3-8B reaches 93.0 percent single-turn Strict Precision under Hybrid-20 conditions, beating rival models.
arxiv-2604-11657: Takaki, Cetinkaya, and Ishii study data poisoning attacks on informativity for observability in data-driven control. An adversary reshapes finite time-series data by an invertible linear map on data matrices. Such maps can embed malicious states into the invariant space explained by the transformed dataset. The authors give an attack method and feasibility rules for when such maps exist. They also formulate an optimization for the smallest-norm attack, measuring the smallest data change needed to destroy it. Tests show small structured maps can invalidate proofs.
arxiv-2604-11757: Ye and nine colleagues present StarVLA-α, a simple strong baseline for studying vision-language-action design choices. VLA models are split across architectures, training data, bodies, and benchmark work. StarVLA-α cuts architectural complexity to reduce confounders, re-testing action modeling, robot pretraining, and interface work. Across joint training on RoboCasa, RoboTwin, SimplerEnv, and LIBERO, the baseline stays competitive, showing a strong VLM backbone with lean design suffices without extra tricks. A single generalist beats π0.5 by 20 percent on the public RoboChallenge.
arxiv-2604-11857: Wakaura removes a key requirement of catalytic quantum error correction, which before needed full knowledge of the ideal target state. His blind version estimates the target from the noisy output alone, turning recovery into a plain estimation problem capped by whether coherent modes survive. With exactly tuned noise, recovery fidelity reaches 0.77 at dimension 64, while a method needing no noise model matches the ceiling within 1.5 percent at dimensions up to 16. A test on hydrogen cuts energy error by a factor of 3.4.
arxiv-2604-11957: Fei and nine colleagues present A-Lab GPSS, a robotic platform making inorganic materials that spoil in air, air-free. An agentic AI framework shapes test design through abductive and inductive logic. In a campaign of 352 samples testing lithium halide spinel ionic conductors, the system hit 72 percent of 171 possible pairings among 19 metals. Mixes with both good current flow and high spinel purity rose from 1.33 percent in the first 75 agent-picked samples to 5.33 percent in the final 75.
arxiv-2604-12057: Slezak and Hagh propose a framework for choosing local rules so desired functions emerge in bottom-up systems, where builders act on stimuli alone. They demonstrate it with a tent-caterpillar silk-network model. Rules can be designed so area coverage, mean line density, and front curvature move toward targets. A statistical approach tunes rule changes to raise the probability of a useful local change, its magnitude, or both. That links local rules to global properties and points toward fabrication by simple builders in uncertain settings.
arxiv-2604-12357: Min and four colleagues present ReflectCAP, reflective note-guided captioning that tackles the tension between factual grounding and fine-grained coverage in detailed image captions. A multi-agent pipeline distills what the target vision-language model hallucinates and overlooks into reusable structured reflection notes. At inference the notes steer the model on both axes, away from known errors and toward overlooked details, jointly improving factuality and coverage. Across eight models it reaches the Pareto frontier on the trade-off and beats model scaling on the quality-cost balance.
arxiv-2604-12557: Subhash Chand Bhoria, Pramod Eyyunni, and Subhrangsu Santra count missing integers in partitions. A missing integer is a positive whole number below the largest part that never appears. The minimal excludant is the smallest such number, revived by Andrews and Newman. The team studies all missing integers across two partition classes. Unrestricted partitions and overpartitions both get full treatment. They count partitions by their number of missing integers. Congruences for two related functions are determined. Three bias-type inequality conjectures are proposed.
arxiv-2604-12757: Arya Shah and two colleagues audit certified robustness fairly across classes. Standard checks need costly attacks or give one aggregate score. GF-Score splits the GREAT Score into per-class profiles. Four welfare metrics measure disparity: disparity index, Gini coefficient, worst-case robustness, and fairness-penalized score. Self-calibration tunes temperature from clean accuracy alone. Tests on 22 RobustBench models across CIFAR-10 and ImageNet show exact splits. Per-class scores expose steady vulnerability patterns, with cat weakest in 76 percent of CIFAR-10 models. More robust models show greater class disparity.
arxiv-2604-12957: Rodrigo Itzamná Becerra-Deana and six colleagues test how polarization steers light through photonic lanterns. Regular lanterns couple ports strongly and symmetrically. Mode-selective lanterns isolate ports and couple weakly. Strongly coupled outputs react sharply to input polarization. Isolated or weakly coupled ports stay nearly polarization independent. The study spans the range from fully symmetric to fully asymmetric lantern designs.
arxiv-2604-13057: Molla and six colleagues classify sentiment in 5,652 English and Bangla reviews of four Bangladeshi government banking apps, filtered from 11,414 raw reviews. Traditional models beat transformer-based ones: Random Forest reaches 0.815 accuracy and Linear SVM 0.804 weighted F1, both above fine-tuned XLM-RoBERTa. Reviewers complain most about slow transactions and poor interface design. eJanata rates worst, and a 16.1-point accuracy gap between Bangla and English text signals a need for low-resource language work.
arxiv-2604-13157: Barrué and 12 colleagues show neural simulation-based inference for proton parton distribution functions, swapping binned fits with full unbinned data. Using the full power of unbinned data avoids information loss from binning, and a proof-of-concept pins down the gluon curve from mock top quark pair output at 13 TeV. With experimental and theoretical systematics counted, the pipeline beats binned fits on precision, pointing toward detector measurements.
arxiv-2604-13257: Soto-Garcia and Chepiga study 1D dual-species Rydberg chains of cesium and rubidium atoms with species-tuned van der Waals interactions. Rivalry between same-species repulsion and cross-species attraction fragments the dynamics, mixing extended frozen regions with local oscillatory sectors, where frozen zones act as barriers shielding orderly dynamics. In the push-only regime, species-picked quenches drive spontaneous fragmentation into cut-off regions with uneven returns, a pattern robust across interaction regimes.
arxiv-2604-13557: Brunet, Melatos, and Rossetto model a magnetic mountain piled on an accreting neutron star once instabilities break ideal magnetohydrodynamics. Mass then drifts across field lines, and their iterative scheme follows the mountain through a sequence of equilibria as accreted mass grows. Cross-field transport stops instabilities from wrecking the mountain: the mass flow adjusts locally, preserving a nonzero mass quadrupole indefinitely without ohmic dissipation.
arxiv-2604-13657: Benvegnen and four colleagues calibrate particle models of ultrasound contrast agents. These agents are tiny gas bubbles that help guide drug delivery with ultrasound. Their shell mechanics shape how they respond to sound. Direct Bayesian inference with dissipative particle dynamics costs too much. So the team uses fast neural-network stand-ins, a staged sampling scheme, and regularization shared across bubble sizes. Fitting published data for Definity and SonoVue pins down key traits such as stretching stiffness and bending modulus.
arxiv-2604-14157: Ampadu proves a derivative-type fixed point theorem for interpolative Berinde weak contractions in ordinary metric spaces. The work builds on Olatinwo's derivative-type framing of the Banach contraction principle and on earlier versions set in multiplicative metric spaces. An example illustrates the main result, and the paper closes by applying it to a Fredholm integral equation.
arxiv-2604-14357: Ching, Zhou, and Zhang present Filament, a static information-flow library for Rust in the Denning style that tracks explicit and implicit flows at variable level without changing the compiler. Type inference trims annotation work for explicit flows, while a small pc_block construct polices implicit flows through a compile-time program-counter label. Macros named fcall and mcall link the library smoothly to ordinary and third-party code. Tests show tiny compile-time cost, modest annotations, and fewer escape hatches than the coarser Cocoon approach.
arxiv-2604-14457: Ben Hmida, Hailemariam, Khan, and Eshete introduce NeuroTrace, a framework and open data set tracing how deep networks handle inputs at inference. Inference provenance graphs capture activation behavior and parameter-driven data flow in a forward pass, giving a structured view of information flow across layers. The package pairs a reproducible extraction engine with a standard graph format for heterogeneous graph networks and a benchmark across vision and malware attacks. Provenance-based detectors separate hostile from benign inputs and transfer across threats, beating prior graph baselines.
arxiv-2604-14657: Recalde's team of six models evacuation destination choices during Hurricane Ian from mobile device location data. They fold Social Vulnerability Index variables into a zone-to-zone demand model at census-tract level. Past survey-based studies suffer recall bias and had urged attention to social vulnerability. Vehicle availability, group-quarters residence, road density, and English proficiency shape both origin departure and arrival appeal. Travel impedance, measured as distance, also matters greatly: evacuees grow far less likely to travel longer distances.
arxiv-2604-15357: Chen and three colleagues introduce FLAME, a method for estimating model inference latency on mobile edge devices under changing processor frequencies. Simple scaling fails because CPU launch work and GPU execution overlap asynchronously, so FLAME models each layer's overlap and pipeline bubbles, then aggregates them. Sparse profiling cuts DNN profiling from hours to minutes and small-language-model profiling from days to minutes, with small errors.
arxiv-2604-15657: Patel, Chhabria, and Arora study where inference-time compute goes in agentic hardware verification and which coverage holes resist closing. Their two-tier Codex plus LangGraph framework taxonomizes holes into methodology-bound ceilings and reasoning frontiers, and tracks tokens across six categories. Domain specialization shifts tokens toward coverage-directed reasoning, reaching 95 to 99 percent coverage with 4 to 13 times fewer tokens and 2 to 4 times faster convergence.
arxiv-2604-15757: Vamplew and Foale flag a missed catch in multi-goal reward learning: with bent payoff rules, the best plan must weigh both the world state and past gains. Plans pack world state plus banked gains into one fat state, which means the agent still needs the gain feed, or a stand-in, once live, even with no more learning. The note spells out why and weighs what that need means in practice.
arxiv-2604-15957: Tërnava and three colleagues present the first empirical study of configurability in small-scale software, programs with limited code or binary size. Analyzing 108 GNU coreutils programs, they find even small programs vary widely, with up to 76 options per program. Run-time variability correlates strongly with codebase size, and across 85 releases of the 20 smallest programs, variability grows over time, mainly from added compile-time options. They coin null-variable software for systems with no configurability beyond mandatory features, arguing that trimming needless variability yields lighter, more maintainable programs.
arxiv-2604-16557: Yan and colleagues unify post-training for large vision-language models with S-GRPO. Supervised fine-tuning forces one expert path and can cause catastrophic forgetting of general skills. Reinforcement learning explores many paths but can collapse at cold start in sparse-reward visual tasks. S-GRPO blends imitation guidance into multi-trajectory exploration, and injects the verified expert path with maximal reward when a group fails fully. That balance speeds convergence, preserves general skills, and beats single-method training on domain adaptation.
arxiv-2604-16757: Bhattacharyya and colleagues evaluate how large language models express social emotions across cultures against human norms. Social feelings serve jobs like claiming independence or building interdependence, varying systematically across cultures. A human study contrasts Euro American and Latin American showing of warm and cool emotions across six frontier models. All models show engaging emotions more than disengaging ones, with starkest gaps for the well-known Euro American persona. Model replies are highly narrow and deterministic, missing human variety, in patterns robust to sampling heat.
arxiv-2604-16957: Vegasena presents Open-TQ-Metal, the first fused compressed-domain attention system for Apple Silicon. It quantizes the key-value cache to four-bit values on the fly and computes attention straight from the compressed form, removing dequantization steps. On a single 64-GB consumer Mac, it runs a 70-billion-parameter model at a 128,000-token context. Attention runs 48 times faster than the dequantize-then-attend baseline, while cache memory shrinks from 40 GB to 12.5 GB.
arxiv-2604-17257: Lee and four colleagues propose REZE, a system curbing shift during domain-tuned vector tuning. Naive contrast tuning on mixed tasks injects task bias with domain knowledge, warping vector shape and harming scores. REZE splits anchor-pair links in an eigen space and gauges spread along each eigen part to find task-variant ways. It applies soft-shrinkage to suppress task noise while keeping stable meaning structure, with no added cost. Across models and benchmarks, REZE beats tuning and post-hoc control in most settings, staying stable where variants collapse.
arxiv-2604-17657: Campanini subjects multiplicity-linked Upsilon(nS) suppression in proton collisions to four detailed tests. CMS measured it at 7 teraelectronvolts, and LHCb measured psi(2S) over J/psi at 13 teraelectronvolts. Cone isolation and transverse sphericity close a scissors constraint: the local Comover Interaction Model reading strains against cone data, its global reading against sphericity data. Non-prompt flatness forces the process to act at early proper times. No hadronic or string-based framework meets all four constraints in published form, leaving an early, globally linked medium as what survives.
arxiv-2604-17957: Pisano and Navigli tackle the cost and errors of process reward model datasets, which judge each reasoning step of language models but usually cover only mathematics. They generate training data from planning problems written in the Planning Domain Definition Language, producing about one million reasoning steps across varied domains. Training reward models on this planned data, added to widely used datasets, yields substantial gains in both mathematical and non-mathematical reasoning across benchmarks. Planning problems thus offer a scalable source of precise, fine-grained step-level training data.
arxiv-2604-18257: Mehta and five colleagues build DocQAC, a system that completes queries while users search inside long documents. Web query completion is well studied, but in-document search adds the document's own text and query history. Their adaptive trie-guided decoder steers a language model toward strong completions with a tunable penalty balancing model confidence and trie guidance. On a new benchmark from ORCAS, the method beats strong baselines and even larger tuned models on seen queries, in seen and unseen documents alike.
arxiv-2604-18457: Carrera and Misguich study how random global pulses prepare states in ring-shaped Rydberg atom arrays. They compare pulse-generated states with Haar-random states inside the relevant symmetry sector. Strong interactions blockade Hilbert-space exploration and cap entanglement growth, yet entanglement-spectrum spacing still matches random-matrix predictions. Weaker interactions approach Haar-like statistics over time, and optimal control in the middle regime prepares target states at high fidelity for nine spins.
arxiv-2604-18757: Leem and four colleagues introduce REVEAL, a system that aligns retinal fundus photos with personal disease-risk profiles to predict Alzheimer's disease and dementia. Risk factors from structured questionnaires are turned into readable narratives for pretrained vision-language models. A group-aware contrastive method pairs patients with similar retinal and clinical traits, linking eye and risk data more tightly. The system predicts disease on average 8 years before diagnosis and beats leading eye-imaging models that use clinical text.
arxiv-2604-19157: Jia and ten colleagues pin down the smallest viable set of 4-bit KV quantization methods for language model serving under constraints such as paged layouts, regular access, and fused attention. Their finding: token INT4 quantization with block Hadamard rotation gives the best trade-off. It recovers nearly all accuracy lost by naive INT4, while vector and Hessian quantization add only marginal gains once compatibility counts. A fused rotation kernel fits into paged layouts with zero measurable overhead, matching INT4 throughput across concurrency levels.
arxiv-2604-19357: Debelak presents FairTree, a method for auditing subgroup fairness in machine learning models, adapted from psychometric invariance testing. Standard tests lean on loss-based scores, which can miss score shifts inside key subgroups. Earlier tools struggle with smooth-valued inputs, but FairTree handles continuous, categorical, and ordinal features directly, with no binning. It also splits score gaps into steady bias and variance, and the paper offers and tests two variants, one shuffle-based and one closer to a model-based test.
arxiv-2604-19757: Pachot and Petit present a transparent screening tool that estimates the environmental impact of running and training current large language models when direct observation is limited. The tool turns plain-language descriptions of applications into bounded environmental figures and feeds a comparative online observatory of market models. Rather than claiming direct measurement of opaque proprietary services, it offers an auditable method tied to sources, aimed at better comparability, transparency, and repeatability.
arxiv-2604-20157: Fang and six colleagues present HumanScore, a test suite for how well AI-made videos show human bodies and motion. Six plain metrics span body-motion truth, time steadiness, and body fit, going past looks alone. Well-planned prompts draw varied moves at mixed strengths from thirteen top video models. The study finds wide gaps between look-truth and body truth, with repeat faults like time jitter, wrong poses, and motion drift, and it ranks models on hard body-based scores.
arxiv-2604-20457: Cao and Li give an efficient polynomial-time method for cluster vertex deletion on chordal graphs. Their result settles an open question raised by Cao and colleagues in 2018, Aprile and colleagues in 2023, Chakraborty and colleagues in 2024, and Hsieh and colleagues in 2024. Their method uses dynamic programming over clique trees, reducing the optimal subproblem value to minimizing a submodular set function. The result closes a gap across four separate research contexts, giving an efficient exact algorithm for this deletion problem on chordal graphs.
arxiv-2604-20757: Jäger, Mandal, Rand, Meggers, and Becker study how sub-bandgap reflectors affect module performance. They estimate how cooling affects annual and cumulative energy yield of silicon modules at locations. An ideal reflector would raise annual yield by about 1 to 2 percent for open-rack modules and by about 2 percent for close-roof modules. Using a simple Arrhenius approach with activation energies under 1 eV, they find that an ideal reflector raises cumulative yield over 30 years by about 2 to 4 percent. That is for an open-rack module in Princeton, New Jersey, USA.
arxiv-2604-21057: Yannis Belkhiter and three colleagues tag each step of a reasoning model's chain of thought so inference can stop once the answer is reached. Their TRACES framework watches step types in real time and finds models shift behavior after landing on a correct answer. Across math and knowledge tests it cuts generated tokens by 20 to 50 percent with similar accuracy, though harder problems demand a more cautious stopping rule.
arxiv-2604-21357: Jian Cui and six colleagues build ReaGeo, a geocoding system that turns coordinates into place names with a language model, replacing multi-stage lookup pipelines. They become geohash strings, turning location guessing into text generation, while step-by-step reasoning sharpens spatial guesses. Learning with a distance-based reward tunes accuracy further. The system handles clear addresses, vague relative locations, and non-point regions, showing broad use.
arxiv-2604-21457: Rajius Idzalika, Muhammad Rheza Muztahid, and Radityo Eko Prasojo build a method for tracking population movement from mobile phone data during disasters, where slow surveys lose time. Uniform movement rules mistake regular commuters for displaced people. Their method sorts mobility types. It spots between-town movement by user type and weekday. It bounds uncertainty from baseline swings with a disaster factor. An Aparri case study after Super Typhoon Nando shows context-aware spotting cutting weekday movement figures by one to three points versus naive methods.
arxiv-2604-21557: Kaito Ninoyu and 21 others present the first high-resolution Cygnus X-1 spectroscopy with XRISM, orbital studies and tentative Fe-K variability. 2024 data track orbital-phase changes with Resolve and Xtend. Resolve reveals ionized iron absorption changes, with orbital changes in column density, ionization state, and blueshifted velocity, suggesting wind structure changes. Intensity-sorted dip spectroscopy suggests changes within a few seconds, matching cooler, denser clumps, though significance is limited. Results hint that wind and disk X-rays may interact within a few seconds, constraining wind-fed accretion.
arxiv-2604-21657: Eike Eberhard and colleagues speed up Kohn-Sham density functional theory by teaching models to propose solver-aligned starting guesses. Earlier models fit ground-state targets well yet slowed convergence on larger molecules, a supervision failure rather than an extrapolation failure. Their solver-aligned initialization learning fixes this by differentiating through the self-consistent field solver. On molecules far larger than the training set, the method cuts iteration counts by roughly a third and delivers a clear wall-time speedup for large drug-like molecules.
arxiv-2604-21857: Roberts and three colleagues use quantum tomography to constrain CP-violating physics beyond the Standard Model, new sources of which are needed to explain the universe's matter-antimatter gap. CP-violating signatures in Standard Model Effective Field Theory hide among CP-even operators in blind observables. They are visible only through interference in the decay angle. Reading the spin density matrix of a diboson system exploits the Beyond-Standard-Model signature, including pure quadratic new-physics terms. This gives better joint sensitivity to CP-even and CP-odd parts.
arxiv-2604-22657: Paudel, Tsai, and Wang propose a hands-off vision-based ID system for group-housed farm animals, capturing 3D point clouds in a feeding station. Accurate ID in group housing is central to livestock care, yet standards rely on RFID ear tags, harmful, loss-prone, and limited by antenna range. Moving past supervised frame-level work, they introduce TARA, the Temporal Adaptive Recognition Architecture, a self-sufficient system keeping identity. TARA updates identity profiles over time to account for body changes in livestock. Label-scarce training uses visit-level votes.
arxiv-2604-22757: Patodiya introduces StratRAG, an open dataset for testing retrieval in question-answering systems that must reason across several documents under noisy conditions. Built from HotpotQA, it holds 2,200 examples across bridge, comparison, and yes-no questions, each paired with fifteen candidate documents holding exactly two gold sources. Hybrid retrieval performs best overall, while bridge questions remain hardest.
arxiv-2604-23657: Kim and colleagues measure the Campbell penetration depth, a probe of true critical current, in a single crystal of the heavy-fermion superconductor CeCoIn5. Its field dependence departs sharply from the usual square-root pattern, with abrupt slope changes at characteristic fields. In a clean sample this points to a change in vortex-lattice symmetry, and the near-linear temperature trend of critical current adds fresh evidence for unconventional superconductivity.
arxiv-2604-23757: Mantovano surveys recent charm and tau physics from the Belle and Belle II experiments, beyond their better-known B physics programme. He reports several never-before-measured charm baryon decay modes, plus new tau studies. Particular emphasis falls on searches for CP violation in tau decays and lepton-flavour violation, including a first search in one tau decay channel.
arxiv-2604-23857: Aswathy and Samanta examine vortex-binary motion with dissipation in a doubly periodic fluid domain. The conservative system reduces exactly to one complex relative coordinate, and a minimal rotated-velocity friction term turns it into a mixed symplectic-gradient flow whose energy decays monotonically. Same-sign vortices spiral outward, while opposite-sign pairs collapse in finite time in the planar limit. On the torus, geometry induces a slow angular drift, and unequal pairs show a distinct nonlinear chirp law.
arxiv-2604-24157: García-Oliva and Lemmen present OxyPOM, a process-based model of oxygen and particulate organic matter with detailed temperature sensitivity. Most models ignore how oxygen removal and production processes respond differently to heat, yet low oxygen threatens aquatic ecosystems. OxyPOM gives each key process, photosynthesis, re-aeration, respiration, mineralization, and nitrification, its own heat response, plus terms for light, grazing, and disease. In a test river-mouth column, detailed heat responses shift season patterns and fix a fourfold undercount of organic carbon production under uniform responses.
arxiv-2604-24257: Cordier and colleagues present the SVOM mission, its profile and system: a French-Chinese observatory launched into low Earth orbit in June 2024 to study transients. Inspired by Swift, it pairs a rapid-slewing satellite with real-time ground links. The space segment combines wide-field ECLAIRs and GRM, both with real-time triggering, plus narrow-field MXT and VT. A visible and infrared ground follow-up system responds promptly to onboard transients. Core, Target of Opportunity, and General Programs serve burst physics and time-domain astronomy.
arxiv-2604-24557: Machado and six colleagues study a rotating two-dimensional gas of ultracold bosons held in a symmetric trap that is not purely harmonic. They follow states from vortex-free clouds to giant vortices with multiple units of circulation, then jolt the interaction strength or trap shape. Entropy measures, mutual information and related tools reveal that chaotic splitting of giant vortices builds many-body correlations, while vortex-free clouds respond with steadier oscillations.
arxiv-2604-24857: Gurrutxaga and colleagues present a Monte Carlo coagulation method for planet-forming disks. It strictly keeps the global stock of dust properties across the disk. Current methods lack strict conservation, so fluctuations can grow and skew predictions. Tests against analytic kernels and a two-dimensional disk benchmark validate it. It reproduces standard results and sharpens the small-grain regime. A water-sublimation test shows strict mass conservation per component.
arxiv-2604-24957: Ousherovitch and Tewari propose Compute Aligned Training, aligning training with test-time strategies for large language models. Standard supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning optimize single-sample likelihood under a base policy. That clashes with test-time procedures that aggregate or filter outputs. By treating inference strategies as operators acting on the base policy, they derive loss functions for those strategies. They build the losses for supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning across test-time strategies. Tests show the method beats standard training substantially on test-time scaling.
arxiv-2604-25057: Niu and Sun present CiteRadar, a citation platform for researcher profiling and map visualization. Citation reach and community shape matter for careers, grants and teamwork, yet accessible tools remain scarce. CiteRadar takes a single Google Scholar ID and outputs a paper list and citing papers. It also gives two ranked tables, a stats summary, and a world map, all from one command. A two-stage author disambiguation system cuts h-index errors up to 9 times the correct value. A URL conversion fix lifts city location data from 0 to about 60 percent.
arxiv-2604-25457: D'Oronzio and four colleagues put forth GramSR, a one-step diffusion super-resolution frame that swaps text conditioning for visual traits from the low-resolution input, pulled by DINOv3. Text captions give only high-level meaning and lack spatially matched detail. GramSR trains three LoRA modules in order: pixel-level for degradation removal, semantic-level for perceptual detail, and texture-level for trait correlation consistency. At run time, guidance scales control degradation removal, semantic gain, and texture keeping. Tests on standard benchmarks show GramSR beats past one-step diffusion ways.
arxiv-2604-25657: Liu and four colleagues design ClayScape, a tool that joins generative AI with clay 3D printing to support Chinese-style ceramic design. Chinese ceramic-making runs through complex linked steps, and digital fabrication still demands CAD and CAM skills. The hybrid workflow blends generative AI with clay printing to open new creative paths. Tests with four creators show the workflow supports accessible creation, expanding exploration while raising tensions around agency and control. The work shows how hybrid workflows can lower digital fabrication barriers.
arxiv-2604-25857: Arnholda and three colleagues embed a slicing agent in a shared open radio unit to identify network slices on the uplink. Beyond-5G and 6G networks need slice-aware service across the radio access network, but the radio unit cannot tell which slice uplink data belongs to. Their agent sorts uplink data into slice-specific radio interface packets through a pipeline with dedicated time-sensitive paths. On an FPGA it handles each packet within two cycles, serving as many as 3822 slices per slot. Tests confirm feasibility and scalability.
arxiv-2604-26657: Kansara, Guo, and Tan introduce a Bayesian optimization framework for inverse design of cellular composites for their full nonlinear mechanical response. Current inverse design leans on large data sets or scarce high-fidelity models and tests, hard for built materials with complex shape-change modes. By blending cheap and dear sources and scoring responses by likeness, the method explores designs fast with fewer tests. Applied to spinodoid composites and checked by crush tests on carbon-fibre strengthened PET-G, it recovers all four targeted responses and beats single-fidelity rivals.
arxiv-2604-27457: Singkanipa, Kasatkin, and Lidar demonstrate exponential quantum speedup for a restricted Simon's problem, where the hidden string's Hamming weight stays below a cutoff, on superconducting processors. Their hardware-aware compilation reduces Simon query circuits to constant depth, needing only nearest-neighbour connections and no overhead. On IBM's Boston and Miami processors, the circuits reach fidelity to show speedup without error suppression. They observe exponential speedup over the classical bound from cutoff four up on Boston and for low-to-intermediate cutoffs on Miami, with polynomial speedup there.
arxiv-2604-27657: Roumesy and four colleagues probe dust in ring-shaped protoplanetary disks through 30 polarized-light images. For each ring system, DRAGyS estimates disk geometry and extracts the scattering phase function, which encodes dust grain properties. Against the AggScatVIR tables, they recover two categories. One falls monotonically, fit by fractal organic or compact aggregates; one is bell-shaped, fit by irregular grains or low-porosity compact aggregates. Average disk flaring comes to about 1.36, but degeneracy is too strong to apply the method to a single disk.
arxiv-2604-27757: Döring, Mohrin, and Skretas introduce Temporally Edge Disjoint Schedule Completion, covering demands by routing k walks through a static graph while staying temporally edge disjoint. They solve the problem in polynomial time. Two restricted variants bound walk distance or time; they present an approximation algorithm and map the landscape in k, h, and size. Restricting the network splits the variants. The distance variant stays hard in k even on a three-vertex path, while the time variant runs in polynomial time on bidirected stars.
arxiv-2604-28157: Wang and colleagues introduce FlashRT, a framework that makes optimisation-based red-teaming of long-context language models cheaper in compute and memory. Attacks such as prompt injection and knowledge corruption are strong but resource-hungry, blocking systematic security testing, especially for academic groups. FlashRT speeds attacks several-fold and cuts GPU memory several-fold against a leading baseline, while applying broadly to black-box optimisation methods.
arxiv-2605-00157:
Lubashan Pathirana develops a theory of forgetting for products of quantum channels, the step-by-step rules that transform quantum states. The central question is when a long chain of such steps washes out all memory of the starting state. Pathirana measures that memory with a trace-Dobrushin coefficient defined for whole products, not single steps.

In the deterministic case, decay of this coefficient turns out to be exactly the condition for the product to act like a moving replacement channel. For random stationary chains, a single exponent governs memory loss, and its negativity matches almost-sure forgetting with fast convergence to a unique replacement channel. Extra mixing assumptions yield even faster average estimates. The results then transfer to inhomogeneous matrix product states, a workhorse description of quantum matter, giving stability and correlation bounds for their infinite-volume limits.
arxiv-2605-00257:
Jatin Gupta and 3 co-authors build an AI assistant for Indian chartered accountancy, a field mixing multi-step arithmetic with dense legal rules. General language models struggle here, and huge models are not practical where computing resources are scarce. Their system, CA-ThinkFlow, pairs a compact reasoning model with retrieval from source documents.

Documents are extracted with a layout-aware tool that keeps their structure, and retrieved passages are added straight into the prompt. The model then reasons step by step in its own chain of thought. On a multi-level accountancy benchmark, the small system reached performance levels matching large proprietary models. Its main weakness remains the hardest regulatory texts, such as those in taxation.
arxiv-2605-00357:
Bokang Wang and 6 co-authors try to make machine learning less scary through hands-on displays. Public views on AI, they note, are clouded by confusion, at a time when daily life leans on these systems more and more. Their hope is that trying things hands-on can spark curiosity, and that curiosity can start a cycle of learning.

The team built three trial displays of machine learning functions, each using hand-picked, open data sets. The trials were built to expose what drawing people in looks like for newcomers, young people included, and people from fields far from tech. Instead of lectures, the work studies what helps newcomers stay curious about new tools. Its stated aim is to shift views away from fear of the unknown and toward calm trust.
arxiv-2605-00557:
James Mooney and 3 co-authors test a counterintuitive claim about research agents: tighter structure in the thinking phase produces more novel science, not less. Language-model research systems usually treat ideation, surveying literature, forming hypotheses, refining reasoning, as a brief prelude. Their framework, SciSense, instead runs ideation as a structured sequence of eight cognitive stages drawn from classic sensemaking research.

They build 120 thousand research trajectories, each conditioned on a paper's citations. In hindsight mode a model reconstructs the path to a known paper; in foresight mode it proposes new directions from the same sources. Models trained on hindsight beat foresight-trained ones on trajectory quality and produced more novel, diverse outputs across every model family tested.
